---
title: "Experimentation Decision System"
subtitle: "Power, guardrails, variance reduction and decision quality"
---

## Executive summary

This case study demonstrates how I would design an experimentation system that
helps product teams make faster decisions without sacrificing validity.

## R: sample size and simulation

```{r}
#| label: experiment-power
#| fig-cap: "Power across candidate sample sizes"

library(tidyverse)
library(pwr)

baseline <- 0.20
relative_mde <- 0.05
treatment <- baseline * (1 + relative_mde)

h <- ES.h(treatment, baseline)

result <- tibble(
  n_per_group = seq(1000, 30000, by = 1000),
  power = map_dbl(
    n_per_group,
    ~ pwr.2p.test(
        h = h,
        n = .x,
        sig.level = 0.05,
        alternative = "two.sided"
      )$power
  )
)

ggplot(result, aes(n_per_group, power)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Sample size required for reliable detection",
    x = "Users per group",
    y = "Statistical power"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## SQL: experiment readout

```sql
WITH assignment AS (
    SELECT user_id, variant, assigned_at
    FROM experimentation.assignments
    WHERE experiment_id = 'onboarding_v2'
),
outcomes AS (
    SELECT
        a.user_id,
        a.variant,
        MAX(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'activation_completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
          AS activated,
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'purchase' THEN e.revenue ELSE 0 END)
          AS revenue
    FROM assignment a
    LEFT JOIN analytics.events e
      ON a.user_id = e.user_id
     AND e.event_at >= a.assigned_at
     AND e.event_at < a.assigned_at + INTERVAL '14 day'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT
    variant,
    COUNT(*) AS users,
    AVG(activated * 1.0) AS activation_rate,
    AVG(revenue) AS revenue_per_user
FROM outcomes
GROUP BY 1;
```

## Decision framework

Ship only when:
1. The primary metric clears the practical decision threshold.
2. Guardrails show no material harm.
3. Instrumentation and randomization checks pass.
4. Results are robust to pre-specified sensitivity analyses.
